scope: Granite4H-tiny is a new sixth-model candidate, not covered by the earlier five-model no-CR zero result. This audit neither establishes benefit nor rejects it. Existing dense GEMV plus host activation/partial sums only; no in-flash nonlinear engine or multi-context extension.

candidate.whole_expert: Once both complete gate/up projections for expert e return, host computes that expert's original activation and releases its down tasks. Other experts' GU need not finish first.
candidate.neuron_chunks: Partition512 hidden neurons into four128-neuron chunks. A chunk depends on its complete128 gate dots and128 up dots, then host SwiGLU, then its down input-column slice. Sum the four down partials before expert scaling/router aggregation under an established numerical contract.
candidate.physical_layout: Each chunk owns matching gate/up rows and down columns. GU paired rows may be physically interleaved for readiness. All dot rows remain complete. Fixed physical chip/plane/block ownership and row alignment must be audited; a ready task cannot relocate weights for free.
candidate.no_cross_nonlinearity_shortcut: No down task may consume a chunk before that chunk's original gate/up dot, scaling and nonlinear product are complete. Chunking does not turn the whole FFN into one linear GEMV.

primary_priors.title: PowerInfer-2: Fast Large Language Model Inference on a Smartphone
primary_priors.read_depth: Personally read sections3.2,4.1.2,4.2-4.4 and implementation section6; Fig6 caption. Not a code execution audit.
primary_priors.evidence: Section4.3 removes matrix barriers at neuron-cluster granularity. Its five stages cover prediction, Gate I/O/compute, then Up/Down I/O/compute, using computing threads and an I/O thread. Section4.4 stores corresponding Gate/Up rows and Down columns together by neuron position.
primary_priors.overlap: Very close prior for host-side neuron producer-consumer scheduling, matching GU/down-neuron layout and cross-matrix execution.
primary_priors.difference: Weights are offloaded from UFS into host memory and computed on CPU/NPU, often with sparsity/cache/prediction. It does not establish ordinary digital NAND GEMV scheduling or AiF command/timing semantics. Dense fixed routing can use the same dependency principle; pipeline itself is not new.

primary_priors.title: SLIM: A Heterogeneous Accelerator for Edge Inference of Sparse Large Language Model via Adaptive Thresholding
primary_priors.evidence: Fused FFN processes a neuron's gate/up vectors and corresponding down contribution before the next neuron, retaining partial sums. Mapping keeps fused vectors page aligned and packs them. Section6.2 interleaves DRAM-PIM/SSD work for two independent input sequences.
primary_priors.overlap: Neuron-granularity GU-to-down dependency execution and ownership coordination are direct architecture prior.
primary_priors.difference: Activation/fusion occurs in its described PE path, rather than repeated host roundtrips. Its two-sequence pipeline is distinct from one token's expert/chunk scheduling. Do not borrow its local-buffer or nonlinear capabilities for AiF.

primary_priors.title: Cambricon-LLM: A Chiplet-Based Hybrid Architecture for On-Device Inference of70B LLM
primary_priors.evidence: Flash GEMV results return to NPU; nonlinear functions reside on NPU. Page-sized2D atoms pipeline array/data/cache registers and PE computation. NPU and flash collaborate on weight GEMVs.
primary_priors.overlap: Existing external nonlinear boundary and page/tile granularity are relevant strong hardware/system prior.
primary_priors.difference: The inspected text does not specify this exact within-expert128-neuron host-release schedule or its placement optimizer. Shared compute-core/plane constraints and its own link timings differ from AiF. Unspecified scheduling is not novelty clearance.

primary_priors.title: AiF: Accelerating On-Device LLM Inference Using In-Flash Processing
primary_priors.read_depth: Original sections4.4,5.1-5.2 and Fig15 personally inspected.
primary_priors.evidence: Output FIFO elements are polled as produced. Section5.1 overlaps attention-head generation with host attention and splits FFN projections between host and SSD before aggregation.
primary_priors.overlap: The original paper already exploits partial readiness and host/SSD tensor-parallel execution.
primary_priors.difference: Its printed schedule does not establish this exact GU/down expert/chunk DAG. Do not assume mid-command prefix callbacks beyond the published native command completion semantics, or that the FIFO disclosure establishes output dtype.

primary_priors.title: FIRM-MoE: Fine-Grained Expert Decomposition for Resource-Adaptive MoE Inference
primary_priors.version: AAAI2026 publisher listing; author PDF inspected excerpt is an anonymous submission version
primary_priors.read_depth: Search tool returned primary author-PDF text for Expert Decomposition, Eq3 and Figs2-3. Direct author PDF opening returned502; publisher page/download returned BotStopper. Not a full-text read.
primary_priors.evidence: Each complete W_gate, W_up or W_down matrix is treated as an independently loadable subexpert; computation queues wait for corresponding weight loads.
primary_priors.difference: The inspected decomposition is by complete projection matrix, not128-neuron slices. No exact match or absence claim about the unread remainder.

G4_inventory.assumptions: H=1536,I=512,K=6,N=16; W8 coefficients;64KiB ordinary four-plane waves; modeled4-byte outputs; actual per-command input payload, no unproved input reuse/broadcast. Counts are derived analytically, not measured hardware.
G4_inventory.qualification: The14-wave floor is an optimistic zero-handoff homogeneous NAND-only schedule bound, not a reachable layout or E2E latency. Average work13.5, route masks,3-wave nonpreemptive GU jobs, finite contexts and dependency release can impose stronger bounds. Extra output service need not all be exposed; shorter input payloads may save service. Apply actual resource scheduling rather than subtracting byte floors as serialized latency.
G4_inventory.granularity_sensitivity: If input DMA/native loads round up to a common minimum, the128-byte versus512-byte input saving may vanish. Published AiF native input and output transfer granularity is not a complete ABI specification.

quantization_dependency.critical_condition: If down A8 uses one dynamic scale computed from maxabs over the entire512-neuron z vector, the first completed128-neuron chunk cannot produce its original quantized input until all chunks finish. This restores a GU-to-down barrier for exact same-quantization execution.
quantization_dependency.existing_conditions_that_can_avoid_it: An already-supported fixed known activation scale, or an existing independently scaled group format whose full group fits a completed chunk. Actual backend support must be established.
quantization_dependency.not_a_free_fix: Choosing separate per-chunk scales changes quantization and requires quality validation; raw integer partials with different scales cannot simply be summed. Do not add a quantization feature under the physical-placement scope.
quantization_dependency.output_contract: GU dot/output scaling must be known before CPU SwiGLU. Down raw output width/overflow/rounding and scale application remain unverified for AiF. Same-expert raw partial integer reduction is conditional on common scale and nonsaturation.

resource_and_latency_bounds.universal_structure: For a fixed legal physical plan, lower-bound makespan by the maximum of: per-chip sensing busy time; per-ECC/PE busy time; per-channel input/output service; PCIe directional service; serialized issue/completion service; CPU worker activation/reduction service; and the weighted longest path in the actual GU-return/activation/quantize/down-return DAG. Include all shared resources with measured or explicitly conditional capacities.
resource_and_latency_bounds.finite_buffer_condition: Ready GU vectors,128-neuron activations, DMA buffers and partial outputs consume host space. In-place streaming may reduce buffering, but must not overwrite data required by outstanding commands. At four chunks, maintaining six1536-element int64 expert accumulators costs73728B, besides staging and model/runtime memory.
resource_and_latency_bounds.first_release: A chunk becomes eligible only after both complete128-row GU dot tasks and host handoff finish. Each described GU task is3waves; output prefix processing is not assumed. Whole-expert jobs use their actual gang/chip completion times.
resource_and_latency_bounds.host_latency_sensitivity: Sweep measured/parametric callback, poll, scatter, scale, activation, quantization and submit latency at least0,0.5,1,2,5,10us per release, with one and bounded multiple host workers. These are sensitivities, not device calibration.
resource_and_latency_bounds.serial_budget_sanity_only: At nominal1.8*28=50.4us NAND headroom, charging the13.824us additional output service serially leaves36.576us before input savings and other costs, or about2.032us per18 extra activation releases. This is a diagnostic budget, not a rigorous no-go: overlap and shared-channel costs determine exposure.

falsifiable_experiments: First run the same resource-aware whole-expert-ready scheduler on old g8GU+g16/down and new g8GU+g12/down; remove the global phase barrier for both. Report placement gain separately from generic pipeline gain.

For chunking, audit each original coefficient exactly once, matching GU row/down-column ownership, complete dot rows, block-contained commands, input bounds and exact byte counts. Compare legal chunk placements against the same best scheduler, including Cambricon-style2D atoms as strong conceptual prior.

Compute zero-host/zero-transfer optimistic DAG makespan first. If this already cannot beat the strongest whole-expert scheduler materially, stop that chunk geometry. Do not reuse an earlier model's zero result.

Add actual input/output/channel/issue service, finite buffers and CPU handoffs; publish break-even overhead curves and per-resource busy/idle traces. Fail the candidate if positive gains survive only free host callbacks, ignored output traffic or unsupported mid-command preemption.

Audit the existing activation quantization dependency. If common dynamic scale requires all z chunks, retain the barrier in the exact run; label any changed-quantization variant separately and keep it outside a strict unchanged-quantizer claim.
Require native numerical output evidence and quality/correctness checks before presenting a functional AiF result. A scheduling simulation can remain a clearly conditional architecture study.
novelty_boundary: Host-mediated neuron producer-consumer execution, paired GU/down neuron storage, and generic ready-task pipelining already have strong primary prior. A possible remaining contribution would need a concrete legal NAND geometry/ownership compiler or placement algorithm that improves dependency-constrained schedules against equally pipelined baselines, with full host/transfer costs and heldout evidence. No breakthrough is established.
